thread:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: KV cache key spillover detected on runtime-pool-3. continuous-batching rate spiked +420% over last 10m. autoscaler (HPA) started oscillating. paging eng-oncall.
ian: saw this too. spike started ~2149497600 (10m). latency P95 up from 120ms -> 650ms for text generation route. dedicated customers seeing timeouts.
sasha: is this the same pattern as last week (prefix buildup)? any sign of a runaway prefill?
ian: similar but different trigger — batch growth correlates with a sudden jump in unique prefix keys (kv_cache_new_keys/s = 48k). looks like a traffic pattern change created many ephemeral prefixes, hitting continuous batching logic and causing huge per-token work.
kevin: copying metrics I'm looking at: batch_size_avg: 64 -> 420, continuous_batch_window_ms: 500 -> 2500, replicas (HPA): 6 -> 18 -> 7 -> 16 (thrash). cpu_util ~ 40-85% oscillating.
maria: customer impact: a handful of Dedicated tenants on region-us-west reported 504s and elevated tail latency. CS notified; ticket INC-5528 opened.
ian: immediate mitigation options:
- disable continuous batching for model-family `redwood-3b-v2` via runtime config (fast).
- roll back last batching config change (revert configmap `batching-config` to yesterday).
- increase HPA stabilizationWindowSeconds + targetUtilization to dampen thrash (medium).

sasha: I'd prefer fast rollback + HPA dampening. disable continuous batching for the specific model to avoid global regressions.
kevin: agree. quick steps: update configmap then trigger rolling restart of runtime pods. patch HPA after rollback.
ian: performing step 1: disable continuous batching on model via api: `curl -XPOST https://control-plane/api/v1/models/redwood-3b-v2/config -d '{"continuous_batching":false}'`

```bash
# quick config rollback
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/runtime --from=configmap/batching-config --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
# or the direct patch
kubectl -n inference patch configmap batching-config -p '{"data":{"continuous_batching":"false"}}'
```

oncall-bot: configmap patch accepted, rollout started. new pods are coming up.
ops-rota: adding HPA patch to reduce thrash: set `stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300` and `behavior.scaleDown.stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300`. will apply after rollback.
kevin: rolling restart completed for 12/14 pods; 2 pods still terminating. Observing batch_size_avg decreasing in 2m window: 420 -> 130.
maria: CS updated customers: applied mitigation, we will monitor for 30m. they asked if any request loss — looks like retries succeeded after backend restored.
ian: digging logs for error spikes. snippet from runtime logs:```
2026-03-15T09:22:46Z runtime-12 ERROR BatchScheduler - request stalled due to kv miss flood (prefix=usr:session:*)
2026-03-15T09:23:12Z runtime-05 WARN KVCache - insert queue length=12000, processing_backlog=true
```
sasha: good catch. This looks like a burst of new sessions/prefixes from a downstream customer test. we should throttle prefill from that tenant or add dedupe on prefixes.
kevin: for now we added ingress rate-limit on the suspected customer route (api key masked: sk-***). applied at edge gateway.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-5528 updated: severity -> S2, assigned -> eng-oncall.

ops-rota: HPA patch applied: stabilization windows set to 300s; targetUtilization bumped 10%. replicas changed: min 4 max 24.

ian: after both actions, replicas stabilized at 9, batch_size_avg ~ 90, P95 latency dropped to ~180ms.
maria: Customer success confirms tail latency improved and no new 504s in last 5 minutes. they want a postmortem if root cause is platform-level.
sasha: handing off to next oncall (ian -> sasha) at 09:45 UTC. I'll keep monitoring for another hour and then follow up with a short incident summary.
ian: notes for post-incident:
- root cause likely traffic pattern causing massive unique prefix churn.
- continuous batching heuristics need guardrails: max per-prefix prefill cap, prefix dedupe, and overflow backpressure.
- HPA config should have longer stabilization for these workloads to avoid thrash.
- consider per-tenant prefill limits and telemetry to correlate bursts to api keys.

kevin: created follow-up tasks: TRACK-870 add per-model continuous_batching toggle in console, TRACK-871 add prefix dedupe, TRACK-872 HPA default stabilization.

maria: CS to coordinate customer debrief and check for any latent errors. tagged INC-5528 in the ticket.

sasha: leaving a short checklist for next hour watcher (ops-rota):
- watch kv_cache_new_keys/s and batch_size_avg (alerts already in place)
- ensure no rollback of config re-enabled continuous batching automatically
- validate HPA doesn't scale down too aggressively (look for >2x replica changes in 5m)
- confirm CS no further reports

ops-rota: acked. I'll watch dashboards and call if anything bounces back. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (partial). watching for stabilization window 30m. will escalate if regressions.

ian: thanks all. leaving follow-up with devex for better observability around prefix cardinality metrics. handing to sasha for postmortem.
sasha: taking it — will produce postmortem draft and link to TRACK tasks. closing chat unless new alerts pop. :wave:
